question.text: Select the function that is continuous at $x=-1.$
question.explanation:
Of the given options, the only one where we can draw the graph of the function without taking our pencil off of the paper in a neighborhood of $x= -1$ is shown below.

All other given options have breaks or asymptotes at $x=-1 $, so it is impossible to draw the function in the neighborhood of $x=-1$ without taking our pencil off of the paper.

example.title: Determining Whether a Function Is Continuous at a Given Point

question.text:
The curve $y=f(x)$ is shown above. At which of the following points is $f(x)$ continuous?

  1. $x=-3$
  2. $x=0$
  3. $x=2$
question.explanation:
Let's consider each point separately.

  • The function $f(x)$ is not continuous at $x=-3.$ Since there is an asymptote at $x=-3,$ it is impossible to draw the function in the neighborhood of $x=-3$ without taking our pencil off of the paper.

  • The function $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=0.$ The graph can be drawn in the neighborhood of $x=0$ without taking our pencil off of the paper.

  • The function $f(x)$ is also continuous at $x=2.$ The graph can be drawn in the neighborhood of $x=2$ without taking our pencil off of the paper.

Hence, the correct answer is "II and III only".

exampleAnswers.title: Determining the Behavior of a Function in the Neighborhood of a Point

question.text:
The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above. Which of the following statements are true?

  1. $f(x)$ is defined at $x=2$
  2. $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \, 2}f(x)$ exists
  3. $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=2$
question.explanation:
By inspecting the graph, we can conclude the following:

  • Statement I is true. Indeed, $f(2)=1.$

  • Statement II is false. Indeed, from the graph we see that \begin{align*} \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,2^-}f(x) &= 1, \\ \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,2^+}f(x) &= -2. \end{align*} Hence, $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \, 2}f(x)$ doesn't exist

  • Statement III is false. The graph of the function breaks at $x=2$ and it's impossible to draw the graph without taking our pencil off of the paper.

question.text:
The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above. Which of the following statements are true?

  1. $f(x)$ is defined at $x=5$
  2. $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \, 5}f(x)$ exists
  3. $f(x)$ has a discontinuity at $x=5$
question.explanation:
By inspecting the graph, we can conclude the following:

  • Statement I is true. Indeed, $f(5)=2.$

  • Statement II is false. Indeed, from the graph we see that \begin{align*} \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,5^-}f(x) &= 2, \\ \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,5^+}f(x) &= 4. \end{align*} Hence, $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \, 5}f(x)$ doesn't exist

  • Statement III is true. The graph of the function has a jump exactly at $x=5$ and it's impossible to draw the graph without taking our pencil off of the paper.
